rationale: The Court is likely to reverse while rejecting a categorical “quote-the-document” rule, instead requiring plaintiffs who rely on internal reports/metrics to plead concrete, particularized substance (what, when, to whom, and contradiction) so Tellabs’s comparative-inference analysis can function. The main fracture points will be whether the majority’s standard effectively becomes a de facto document-production requirement and how sharply to cabin expert opinions as substitutes for pleaded facts.
